subject: science
passage: Psychologist Ingrid Halvorsen taught two groups of adults a list of words from a language none of them spoke. Both groups were tested on the words twelve hours later, when everyone was fully awake. One group learned the words at 9 p.m. and slept through the night before the test; the other learned them at 9 a.m. and stayed awake through the day. Although the time between learning and testing was the same for both groups, the group that had slept remembered noticeably more words. These results suggest that ______
stem: Which choice most logically completes the text?

choices.A: sleeping soon after learning may help people retain new words.
choices.B: adults remember familiar words better than unfamiliar ones.
choices.C: people can learn new words only while they are asleep.
choices.D: staying awake after learning helps memory more than sleep does.

explanation.why: Both groups had the same twelve-hour gap before the test, but only one group slept during it, and that group remembered more. The sleep after learning is therefore a likely reason for their better memory.
explanation.A: Correct. With the delay held equal, the group that slept after learning retained more of the words.
explanation.B: Incorrect. Everyone learned unfamiliar words, so the study made no comparison with familiar ones.
explanation.C: Incorrect. Both groups learned the words while awake; the study tested memory after sleep, not learning during it.
explanation.D: Incorrect. This reverses the result; the group that slept remembered more.
